To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Danckwerts’s expression allows the computation of transient currents for an EC’ mechanism, and that for the inlaid microdisc electrode the transient currents tend to the cotrellian behaviour as t tends to zero, regardless of the shape or size of the microelectrode.

the transient limiting current of a first-order EC reaction can be computed from the limiting current at the same electrode in the absence of homogeneous reaction and that, for an inlaid or recessed microdisc, the transient limiting current is independent of the electrode size and geometry, and tends to the planar behaviour when time tends to zero.
Danckwerts expression allows the calculation of the limiting current for an EC’ mechanism from the limiting currents for the same electrode in the absence of homogeneous reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of transient currents at the microdisc electrode in the presence of a first-order homogeneous reaction regenerating the species being electrochemically oxidised or reduced.
the application of Danckwertz’ expression to first order EC’ reaction.
a general method to obtain the transient limiting current at any microdisc electrode from the limiting currents when there is no reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Danckwerts expression provides a useful tool to study the transient behaviour of a first-order EC′ reaction, and it can be used to estimate the time required for the system to reach a steady-state, as well as to compute the kinetic parameter from experimental data.

, for a homogeneous reaction of the type EC’ (where C and C′ are the reactant and product, respectively) the transient currents at a microelectrode of arbitrary shape, size and location, can be predicted from the limiting currents obtained at the same electrode without homogeneous kinetics.
the Danckwerts expression is a general tool for the analysis of transient currents at electrodes of arbitrary geometry and hydrodynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the limiting currents at an inlaid microdisc electrode with a homogeneous first order reaction regenerating the species are always higher than the corresponding currents at the recessed electrode, and the difference increases with the electrode size and the kinetic constant.

, for a first-order homogeneous reaction, the transient current at the inlaited electrode is always larger than the steady-state one and the transient current at a recessed electrode is always smaller.

Danckwerts’s expression allows to compute transient currents in any system, with any electrode shape, from steady-state currents at the same system, provided the electrode shape is not changed during the experiment and the hydrodynamic regime remains the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Danckwerts method can be used to obtain the kinetic constant in a first order EC′ reaction, from the limiting current at a microdisc electrode.
the transient currents are not affected by the shape of the microelectrode.
the transient limiting current at an inlaid electrode is always larger than the corresponding one at the recessed microdisc, for all values of the kinetic constant and the electrode size.
